transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks. Um, I guess I'm here because for a really long time now, I’ve just been walking around with this... this flat, heavy feeling. Like, even when work is going okay. I'm a management analyst, and we just had this massive project where I had to overhaul a client's entire data pipeline. They were still using this legacy software from like, 2014, which is honestly just wild to me that a company that size wouldn't update their systems. The guy I was working with, Dave, he kept trying to tell me it was fine, but it was just so incredibly slow and crashed every time we pulled a report. 

But anyway... even when I fix something like that, and I get a win, or people are nice to me about it, I still just feel down and kind of empty most days. I just can't seem to shake it.
How long have you been feeling this flat, heavy feeling?

Um, I guess it's been... probably about two years and two months now. It started right around the time this dashboard project put me in the spotlight at work. Which, honestly, I didn't even want that much attention. I just built this automated dashboard for the regional managers because they were always complaining about tracking their KPIs, and suddenly the VP is calling my name out in the quarterly all-hands meeting. I had to stand up and wave and everything, which I hate. I'm only 22, I haven't even finished my college degree yet, so having all these senior guys staring at me and expecting me to speak was just... a lot. My manager meant well, but she kept scheduling me for all these cross-departmental presentations after that. I even had to buy a new suit for one of them, and the tailor totally messed up the hem on the pants, so I had to go back to the mall twice just to get it fixed before the presentation. It was a whole annoying ordeal. But yeah... ever since that whole dashboard thing blew up, I've just had this constant heavy feeling.
Do you still enjoy activities or hobbies that you used to find pleasurable before this flat, heavy feeling started?

Um... I don't really know if I enjoy them less. I guess I haven't really thought about it. I used to play a lot of video games, mostly these really long RPGs where you have to grind for hours just to get a specific sword or whatever. I spent like three weeks trying to get this one rare drop in Final Fantasy, and the drop rate was supposed to be 5%, but I swear the RNG was broken because I killed the same boss probably two hundred times. I even started keeping a spreadsheet of my attempts, because, you know, I'm an analyst, I can't help it. And I found this forum post from 2018 where this guy was convinced the drop rate was tied to the in-game clock, so I tried syncing my attempts to midnight server time, which meant I was staying up till like 3 AM on a Tuesday. My roommate at the time got so annoyed because my mechanical keyboard is really loud. He actually threatened to pour coffee on it once. But yeah... I don't know, I guess I just don't play as much anymore.
Do you feel like you get as much pleasure from playing video games as you used to?

Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. Like I said, I haven't really thought about if it's less fun or whatever. I just... I haven't been playing much. Actually, my PlayStation controller broke a couple of weeks ago. The right bumper just completely snapped off. I was playing this racing game and I guess I hit it too hard, but honestly, the build quality on those controllers has gone way downhill since the PS3 era. I tried looking up how to fix it on YouTube, and this guy had a whole 40-minute tutorial, but he was using all these specialized tiny screwdrivers that I don't have. I went to Home Depot to see if I could buy a kit, but the guy working in the hardware section was completely useless. He tried to sell me a standard Phillips head set, and I was like, dude, do you even know what a Torx screw is? It was so frustrating. I ended up just ordering a new controller on Amazon, but it got delayed in shipping because of some weather thing in the Midwest. So yeah... I don't know if I enjoy games less. I just haven't been playing.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... I don't really think so. I mean, I guess I'm just not doing as much stuff, but it's not like I don't care about it anymore. Like, I used to go to this trivia night at a pub down the street with some guys from work. We had this really good team name, "The Excel-erators," because, you know, we're analysts. But then the pub changed their menu and got rid of these really good jalapeño poppers they used to have. They replaced them with these weird artisanal pretzel bites that cost like twelve dollars, which is just ridiculous for pretzels, you know? And the new trivia host was this guy who thought he was a stand-up comedian, but his jokes were just terrible. He kept doing this awful Christopher Walken impression every time he read a history question. It got so annoying that my buddy Dave actually went up to him during the break and asked him to stop, which made things super awkward for the rest of the night. So we just stopped going after that. But yeah, it's not that I lost interest in trivia or anything, it's just... circumstances, I guess.
Do you feel like things that used to give you pleasure no longer do?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like things are less pleasurable, really. Like I said, I'm just not doing them as much right now. It's funny you ask that though, because I was actually just talking to my mom about pleasure and stuff the other day. She called me on Sunday morning, right when I was trying to make breakfast. I was making these pancakes from scratch—not from a mix, because I watched this cooking show where they explained how the chemical leaveners in the boxed mixes can leave a weird metallic aftertaste. So I bought buttermilk and everything. But she called right as I was pouring the batter into the pan, and my phone was on the counter, so I had to answer it on speaker. And she started going on and on about how my cousin just bought a boat, and how he's always out on the lake having fun, and she was like, "Why don't you do fun things anymore?" And I was trying to explain to her that I just didn't want a boat, but then I got distracted and the first batch of pancakes completely burned. Like, black on the bottom. It set off the smoke detector, which is super sensitive because it's right near the kitchen door, and my cat freaked out and hid under the sofa for like three hours. So yeah... I don't know, I just... I don't think I've lost pleasure in things. I just haven't been doing them.
Do you often feel tired or have low energy?

Um... yeah, I guess I do feel pretty tired a lot. Like, by the afternoon I'm just so wiped out that even fixing a simple spreadsheet error or finishing my expense paperwork feels like I'm dragging my body and my brain through mud. It's the same with getting myself to play soccer, which I used to do every Tuesday. The fields we play at are over by the old high school, but they recently redid the turf, and honestly, I hate it. The turf beads get everywhere—like, in my cleats, in my car, I even found some in my washing machine last week. It made this horrible grinding noise during the spin cycle, and I thought I was gonna have to call a repair guy. Do you know how much appliance repair costs these days? It's a total scam. They charge a hundred dollars just to show up and look at the thing, and then they tell you it's cheaper to just buy a new one. My buddy Steve had that happen with his fridge, and he ended up having to live out of a cooler for a week while he waited for a new one to get delivered. But yeah... I just feel really, really tired by the time the afternoon rolls around.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I sleep okay, I think. I usually try to get into bed around eleven, but lately I've been getting sucked into these YouTube rabbit holes. The other night I started watching this video about how they restore old cast iron skillets. It's actually crazy how rusty they can get, and these guys use electrolysis tanks to strip all the gunk off. It made me want to go to a thrift store and see if I could find a vintage Griswold pan, because supposedly the old ones have a much smoother cooking surface than the new ones you buy at the store. The new ones are all pebbly, you know? Anyway, I was looking up thrift stores in my area on my phone, and I noticed that the Goodwill down on 4th Street closed and turned into one of those popup Halloween stores. Which is weird because it's only August. Who buys a Halloween costume in August? But yeah, my sleep is fine, I guess. I just... I don't know, I haven't really noticed any problems with it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite?

Um... no, my appetite is pretty much the same, I think. I mean, I still eat my normal meals. I did go to this new sandwich place for lunch yesterday, though. It's right next to my office, where that old dry cleaner used to be. I was kind of sad when the dry cleaner closed because the guy who ran it, Mr. Henderson, always gave me a discount on getting my suits pressed. But this new sandwich shop is supposed to be really good. They bake their own bread every morning, and you can smell it all the way down the street. I got this turkey club, but they put some kind of weird aioli on it instead of regular mayo. It had a really strong garlic flavor, which I guess is fine, but I had a meeting with the regional manager right after lunch, and I was so paranoid that my breath smelled like garlic the whole time. I even tried chewing a piece of that cinnamon gum, but cinnamon and garlic do not mix well. It tasted like a candle was burning in my mouth. So I just tried to breathe through my nose during the meeting. But yeah, my appetite hasn't really changed or anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um... no, not really. I don't think my weight has changed. My clothes still fit the same, mostly. Except for this one pair of khakis I bought last month from that outlet mall out by the interstate. Have you been out there recently? They added a whole new section with a bunch of designer stores, but the parking is a total nightmare. I spent like twenty minutes just driving up and down the rows looking for a spot, and I finally had to park all the way over by the food court. Which normally I wouldn't mind, but it was pouring rain, and of course I forgot my umbrella in my other car. I always do that. I leave it in the backseat of my sedan, but I took my roommate's SUV that day because I was supposed to pick up a bookshelf from IKEA later. IKEA is another place where you just lose all sense of time, you know? You walk in for a bookshelf, and suddenly it's three hours later and you're eating Swedish meatballs and buying fake potted plants. But yeah... no, my weight is pretty much the same, I haven't noticed any difference.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel about yourself or your self-worth over the past two years?

Um... I don't know, I guess I've just been feeling pretty down on myself. Like, people at work still bring up this one dashboard I built, and honestly, my first thought is always that I somehow just fooled them all into thinking I know what I'm doing. 

Which is funny because the software we use for those dashboards just got this massive update last week, and it completely changed the user interface. They moved the export button from the top right to the bottom left, which makes zero sense from a design perspective. I was reading this article about UX design the other day, and it was saying how users instinctively look to the top right for action buttons because of how early web browsers were set up. It’s like how we still use a floppy disk icon for "save" even though I don't think I've ever even used a real floppy disk in my entire life. My dad had a whole box of them in our basement, though. He used to play this ancient text-based adventure game on them where you had to type "go north" or "pick up key" and stuff. I tried playing it once but I just kept dying in this virtual cave because I couldn't figure out how to light a lantern. 

But um... yeah, what was I saying? Oh, right. With work. It just feels like every single time I miss a follow-up or send an email a little late, it's just undeniable proof that I'm not actually as capable as they all think I am.
Have you ever thought about death or wanted to die?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't sit around wishing I was dead or anything like that. I just... I don't know, sometimes I just feel really tired, you know? Like that kind of tired where sleep doesn't actually fix it. 

I was actually trying to fix my sleep schedule last week because I read this whole thread online about circadian rhythms and how blue light from screens messes with your melatonin production. So I bought these blue-light-blocking glasses off Amazon. They have these really thick, orange lenses, and I look absolutely ridiculous wearing them. My roommate walked in while I was watching TV with them on and he just started laughing so hard he spilled his water. Which reminds me, we still haven't gotten our water filter fixed. The landlord said he was going to send a guy out on Tuesday, but nobody ever showed up. It's so frustrating because we have to keep buying those big plastic jugs from the grocery store, and they're so heavy to carry up three flights of stairs. I usually try to carry two at a time to save trips, but the plastic handles dig into my hands so badly. I should probably get some of those grip pads they use for weightlifting. My buddy from high school got really into powerlifting recently, and his entire Instagram feed is just him deadlifting in his garage... 

But um... yeah, no, I haven't really had any thoughts about dying or anything like that. Just... just tired mostly.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things you've done or haven't done?

Um... yeah, I guess I do feel guilty sometimes. Like I'm just not doing enough, you know? Especially with my friends. I keep blowing off plans because I just don't have the energy to go out. 

Like last weekend, my buddy Dave invited me to this big barbecue he was hosting. He just bought a new house out in the suburbs, one of those places with a huge backyard and a built-in fire pit. He's been talking about this fire pit for months. He even bought this special kind of wood that's supposed to smell like cedar when it burns. I don't know much about wood, honestly. My grandpa used to whittle these little wooden birds out of pine when I was a kid. He had this whole collection of them lined up on his mantelpiece, right next to this old grandfather clock that chimed every hour. The chimes used to scare me when I stayed over, especially at night. It's funny how things that seem so loud when you're little don't really bother you when you get older. Kind of like how I used to hate the taste of black coffee, but now I drink it every morning. I started going to this new coffee shop near my apartment, actually. The barista there has this crazy blue hair, like neon blue... 

But um... what was the question? Oh, right, feeling guilty. Yeah, I just... I feel bad that I keep canceling on people, but I just can't seem to make myself go.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Um... no. No, I haven't wanted to hurt myself or anything like that. I don't really get thoughts like that. 

I did actually cut my hand pretty bad the other day, though, but it was a total accident. I was trying to open one of those hard plastic blister packs that literally everything seems to come in nowadays. It was for a new computer mouse, actually. My old one started doing this weird double-clicking thing every time I pressed the left button, which was driving me absolutely insane when I was trying to highlight cells in Excel. Do you know how hard it is to build a pivot table when your mouse keeps unselecting everything? Anyway, I was using these kitchen shears to open the packaging, and they slipped. They're these really heavy-duty shears I got from a thrift store a few years ago. I love thrift stores, you can find the most random stuff there. I found this vintage bowling shirt once that had the name "Earl" embroidered on the pocket. I wore it to a Halloween party last year and told everyone I was a professional bowler. I even learned how to keep score on paper, which is surprisingly complicated with all the strikes and spares and frames...

But um... yeah, no, I haven't ever thought about doing anything to hurt myself on purpose. Just... just the usual clumsiness, I guess.
Do you have trouble concentrating on things?

Um... concentrating? I mean, maybe a little? It's hard to say. I guess I do zone out sometimes when I'm working. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to be running this data analysis for my manager. We use this software that takes forever to load, so you just sit there watching this little loading bar creep across the screen. It reminds me of back when we had dial-up internet at my mom's house. You'd hear that awful screeching sound, and then it would take ten minutes just to load a single picture. My brother and I used to fight over the phone line all the time because he always wanted to call his girlfriend right when I was trying to play Runescape. He actually just married that girl last month. They had this huge outdoor wedding, but it rained the entire time. The caterers had to move all the food into this tiny tent, and everyone was bumping into each other trying to get to the buffet. They served these little crab cakes that were actually pretty good, though. I'm usually not a big seafood guy. I got food poisoning from some bad shrimp at a buffet once in college, and it completely ruined it for me. I couldn't even look at the ocean for like a year without feeling a little sick to my stomach...

But um... yeah, I guess I do get distracted sometimes. I don't know if it's worse than normal, though. Just... my mind wanders, I guess.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

Um... moving slowly? Or restless? I don't... I don't really think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that. 

I mean, I sit at a desk most of the day, so I'm not really moving around a lot anyway. We just got these new ergonomic chairs at the office, actually. They're supposed to be really good for your posture, but honestly, it just feels like sitting on a weird, bumpy exercise ball. My old roommate had one of those exercise balls instead of a chair. He was super into fitness, always talking about core strength and macros and stuff. He used to make these protein shakes that smelled like wet dog and chalk. He tried to get me to drink one once, and I swear I couldn't taste anything else for the rest of the day. We used to live in this tiny apartment above a dry cleaner. You could always smell the chemicals coming up through the floorboards, especially in the summer when it got really hot. We didn't have AC, just this one box fan that we'd stick in the window. It made this loud rattling noise, but it was better than nothing. I actually saw him the other day, my old roommate I mean. He was at the grocery store, buying like, five cartons of eggs. I don't know who needs that many eggs at once...

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, I don't think I'm moving slower or feeling restless or anything. Just... just normal, I guess.
Do you feel like you're able to move around and do physical things at the same pace as you used to?

Um... yeah, I think so? I mean, my pace feels about the same as it always has. I haven't really noticed feeling slower or anything when I'm doing physical stuff. 

I actually tried to start running a couple weeks ago. I went to the mall and bought these really expensive running shoes. They're bright neon green. The guy at the shoe store said they reflect light for night running, which I guess is safe, but they're so bright they kind of hurt your eyes in the daylight. He was this really intense guy, too, kept talking about his marathon times and his resting heart rate. He kind of reminded me of my high school gym teacher who used to make us run bleachers in the rain. I absolutely hated the bleachers. Once I slipped and scraped my shin so bad on the metal edge that I still have a scar. It actually looks a little bit like the state of Florida if you squint at it right. I've never even been to Florida, though. My aunt lives down in Tampa and she keeps inviting me to visit, but she has like six cats and I'm super allergic. The last time I was around a cat, my eyes swelled up so bad I looked like I had gone ten rounds in a boxing ring. I had to take Benadryl and just sleep for like fourteen hours straight... 

But um... wait, what was the question? Oh, doing physical things. Yeah, no, I think I move at a pretty normal pace. Nothing's really changed there.
Do you often feel worthless?

Um... worthless? I don't know if I'd use that exact word, but I definitely feel like a fraud a lot of the time. Like, people at work still bring up this one dashboard I built a while ago, and my first thought is always that I somehow just fooled them all into thinking it was good. And then every time I miss a follow-up or send a late email, it just feels like proof that I'm not actually as capable as they think I am. 

Speaking of emails, our company's spam filter has been acting completely crazy lately. It keeps sending actual important stuff to junk, but then letting through these weird phishing scams. I got one last week that said it was from the CEO asking me to go buy Apple gift cards for a client presentation. Which is exactly how my grandfather got scammed out of like two thousand dollars last year. He drove all the way to Walgreens and bought a huge stack of them because someone called him pretending to be from the IRS. My mom was so mad. She spent like three days on the phone with his bank trying to get it sorted out. She actually works at a bank—well, a credit union, as a loan officer. She's always complaining about the interest rates and how nobody is buying houses right now. I guess the housing market is pretty terrible everywhere, though. A guy I went to college with just bought a house, but it's basically a total teardown. He posts all these DIY renovation videos on Instagram, but half the time he's just breaking things worse. He tried to install his own plumbing and ended up flooding his entire basement...

But um... sorry, what did you ask me? I completely lost my train of thought. Was it about my job?
Have you had periods of feeling down or depressed like this before?

Um... before? I don't really know. I mean, maybe? I guess I've just felt kind of... like this for a long time, so it's hard to say if there were specific periods or if it's just always been there. It just feels like a blur.

Speaking of blurs, I forgot to wear my glasses today. My prescription is pretty mild, so I can usually get by without them, but by the end of the day, I always get this terrible headache right behind my eyes. I really need to go to the optometrist and get my prescription checked. The last time I went, the doctor had this machine that blew a puff of air right into my eyeball. I hate that thing. It always makes me jump, and then they have to do it again. The receptionist there was really nice, though. She had this huge collection of enamel pins on her lanyard. One of them was a tiny avocado with a smiley face on it. It reminded me of this avocado toast I had at a brunch place downtown a few weeks ago. It was ridiculous—they charged like eighteen dollars for one slice of bread and half an avocado, and they didn't even toast the bread all the way through. It was just soggy in the middle. My friend who I went with actually sent hers back, which I could never do. I hate confrontation. I'd rather just eat the soggy bread than make a scene. She's always been like that, though, super assertive. She actually just got promoted to regional manager at her company, which means she gets a company car. It's just a standard white sedan, but still, free gas...

But um... sorry, I drifted off again. What were we talking about? Oh, feeling down before. Yeah, I don't know if I've had periods of it, really. Just feels like this is kind of how things are.
Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself or wished you were dead?

Um... no, no I haven't ever thought about hurting myself or... wishing I was dead. I mean, things feel kind of heavy and dull a lot, but I've never actually wanted to... you know, end it or anything. 

It's kind of like... I don't know, like when my car wouldn't start last winter. I have this old Honda Civic, and the battery just completely died on the coldest day of the year. I was stuck in the parking lot at work for like three hours waiting for a tow truck. The tow truck driver was this huge guy with a giant beard, and he was listening to the most intense heavy metal music I've ever heard. He told me he plays bass in a band on the weekends and they were going on tour in Europe. I always wonder how people afford to do stuff like that. Like, touring Europe has to be so expensive, right? I've only been out of the country once, to Mexico for a friend's wedding. It was supposed to be this beautiful beach ceremony, but a hurricane rolled in the day before and we had to do the whole thing in the hotel conference room. It smelled like stale coffee and chlorine from the indoor pool next door. They tried to make it nice with all these fake palm trees, but it just looked like a high school prom. My suit got completely ruined on the walk from my room to the conference center because the wind was blowing the rain sideways. I tried to get it dry cleaned when I got back, but the dry cleaner near my apartment closed down. They turned it into one of those fancy dog bakeries where they sell cupcakes made out of liver and sweet potatoes...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, right, thoughts of hurting myself. Yeah, no. I don't have thoughts like that.
